turn1.explanation: The unit fires on the token just before a period, most strongly when the period is an internal separator rather than a sentence end: decimal points, URL/domain dots, code member access, abbreviations and citation numbers. It fires more weakly on tokens before ordinary sentence-ending periods.
turn1.evidence: Top activations sit right before dots in decimals (-0.07, 29.9), domains (www., github.com), code (e.target.classList, params.delete), and abbreviations (N.C., R. 47.5, i.e., U.S.); 'recognized.The' with no space reaches 9. Plain sentence-final cases ('have.', 'gaming.', 'window.') appear only in the mid range at about 5-6.
turn1.missing_data: Activations on tokens before periods versus other punctuation in matched contexts, plus activation on the period token itself, would confirm that the unit predicts a following '.' rather than responding to numeric or URL content.
